partA.text: Three resistors of 6 Ω, 3 Ω and 2 Ω are connected in parallel. The equivalent resistance is:
In a purely capacitive AC circuit, the current:
partA.explanation: For a capacitor, i = C dv/dt, so current leads voltage by 90°.

partA.text: Thevenin's theorem replaces a linear two-terminal network by:
options: A current source in parallel with a resistance
A voltage source in series with a resistance
partA.explanation: Thevenin equivalent is Vth in series with Rth.

partA.text: The Q-factor of a series RLC circuit at resonance is given by:
partA.explanation: Q = ωL/R = 1/(ωCR) for a series resonant circuit.

partA.text: Maximum power transfer from a source to a load occurs when load resistance equals:
partA.explanation: Maximum power transfer theorem: RL = Rs (source internal resistance) for DC resistive networks.

partA.text: The unit of admittance is:
partA.explanation: Admittance Y = 1/Z is measured in Siemens (mho).

partA.text: In a series RLC circuit at resonance, the impedance is:
partA.explanation: At resonance XL = XC, so they cancel, leaving Z = R, minimum and purely resistive.

partA.text: Norton's equivalent circuit consists of:
options: Voltage source in series with resistance
Current source in parallel with resistance
partA.explanation: Norton equivalent is a current source IN in parallel with RN (= Rth).

partA.text: The time constant of an RC series circuit is:
partA.explanation: Time constant τ = RC for a charging/discharging RC circuit.

partA.text: The depletion region in a p-n junction diode acts as:
options: Both an insulator and forms a capacitance
partA.explanation: The depletion region has no free carriers (insulating) but also forms a junction capacitance that varies with bias.

partA.text: In a forward-biased silicon diode, the typical cut-in (knee) voltage is approximately:
partA.explanation: Silicon diodes have a typical forward cut-in voltage of about 0.7 V; germanium is about 0.3 V.

partA.text: A Zener diode is normally operated in:
partA.explanation: Zener diodes are designed to operate in reverse breakdown for voltage regulation.

partA.text: The current gain β of a BJT is defined as:
partA.explanation: β (common-emitter current gain) = IC/IB.

partA.text: Which configuration of BJT amplifier provides voltage gain, current gain, but 180° phase shift?
partA.explanation: Common emitter (CE) provides both voltage and current gain with 180° phase inversion.

partA.text: An enhancement type MOSFET conducts when:
partA.explanation: E-MOSFET requires VGS > VT to create a conducting channel; it is normally OFF.

partA.text: The early effect in a BJT refers to:
options: Variation of base width with collector-base voltage
Increase in emitter current with temperature
Reduction of gain at high frequency
partA.explanation: Early effect: base-width modulation as VCB increases, affecting output characteristics.

partA.text: In an ideal op-amp, the input impedance is assumed to be:
partA.explanation: Ideal op-amp characteristics: infinite input impedance, zero output impedance, infinite gain.

partA.text: A photodiode is normally operated in:
partA.explanation: Photodiodes are reverse biased so photogenerated carriers increase reverse leakage current proportionally to light.

partA.text: For an ideal op-amp in inverting configuration with Rf and Rin, the closed-loop gain is:
partA.explanation: Inverting amplifier gain Av = -Rf/Rin.

partA.text: The gain of a non-inverting op-amp amplifier with feedback resistor Rf and input resistor R1 is:
partA.explanation: Non-inverting amplifier gain Av = 1 + Rf/R1.

partA.text: A class B power amplifier has a theoretical maximum efficiency of approximately:
partA.explanation: Class B push-pull amplifiers have a maximum theoretical efficiency of about 78.5% (π/4).

partA.text: Negative feedback in an amplifier:
options: Has no effect on gain stability
partA.explanation: Negative feedback trades gain for improved bandwidth, reduced distortion, and gain stability.

partA.text: The CMRR of a differential amplifier is defined as the ratio of:
partA.explanation: CMRR = Ad/Acm, ideally infinite for a perfect differential amplifier.

partA.text: An oscillator circuit must satisfy the Barkhausen criterion, which requires loop gain magnitude equal to:
partA.explanation: Barkhausen criterion: loop gain |Aβ| = 1 and total phase shift = 0° (or 360°) for sustained oscillation.

partA.text: A Wien bridge oscillator is commonly used to generate:
partA.explanation: The Wien bridge oscillator is a classic RC oscillator producing sinusoidal output in the audio range.

partA.text: In a voltage regulator using a series pass transistor, the transistor operates in:
partA.explanation: Series regulators keep the pass transistor in the active region to control the voltage drop continuously.

partA.text: The slew rate of an op-amp is defined as:
options: Maximum rate of change of output voltage
partA.explanation: Slew rate = maximum dVout/dt the op-amp output can achieve, expressed in V/µs.

partA.text: The number of NAND gates required to realize an AND gate is:
partA.explanation: AND = NAND followed by another NAND used as an inverter, so 2 NAND gates.

partA.text: A full adder circuit has how many inputs and outputs?
partA.explanation: Full adder: inputs A, B, Cin; outputs Sum and Cout — 3 inputs, 2 outputs.

partA.text: A JK flip-flop with J=K=1 on each clock pulse will:
partA.explanation: J=K=1 causes the JK flip-flop to toggle state on each clock edge.

partA.text: The minimum number of flip-flops needed to build a MOD-10 (decade) counter is:
partA.explanation: 2^4=16 ≥ 10, and 2^3=8 < 10, so 4 flip-flops are the minimum needed.

partA.text: A multiplexer with 8 input lines requires how many select lines?
partA.explanation: n select lines address 2^n inputs; 2^3 = 8, so 3 select lines are needed.

partA.text: The Boolean expression A + AB simplifies to:
partA.explanation: By absorption law, A + AB = A.

partA.text: In K-map simplification, a group of 4 adjacent 1s is called a:
partA.explanation: A group of 2 cells is a pair, 4 cells is a quad, 8 cells is an octet.

partA.text: A ripple counter is also known as:
partA.explanation: Ripple (asynchronous) counters have flip-flops triggered by the output of the previous stage, not a common clock.

partA.text: The number of bits required to represent the decimal number 255 in binary is:
partA.explanation: 255 in binary is 11111111, which uses 8 bits.

partA.text: A system is said to be causal if its output at any time depends on:
partA.explanation: Causal system: output at time t depends only on present and past input values, not future ones.

partA.text: The Fourier transform of a unit impulse δ(t) is:
partA.explanation: The Fourier transform of δ(t) is 1 for all frequencies (flat spectrum).

partA.text: The region of convergence (ROC) of the Laplace transform of a causal signal lies:
options: To the left of the rightmost pole
To the right of the rightmost pole
partA.explanation: For causal signals, ROC is to the right of the rightmost pole in the s-plane.

partA.text: Convolution of a signal x(t) with δ(t-t0) results in:
partA.explanation: Convolving with a shifted impulse shifts the signal: x(t) * δ(t-t0) = x(t-t0).

partA.text: The Nyquist sampling rate for a signal band-limited to fm Hz is:
partA.explanation: Nyquist rate = 2fm to avoid aliasing when sampling a band-limited signal.

partA.text: A system is LTI (linear time-invariant) if it satisfies:
partA.explanation: LTI systems must satisfy both the superposition (linearity) property and time invariance.

partA.text: The z-transform of a discrete unit step signal u[n] has ROC:
partA.explanation: Z-transform of u[n] is z/(z-1) with ROC |z| > 1.

partA.text: Energy signals have:
options: Finite energy and finite average power
Finite energy and zero average power
Infinite energy and finite average power
partA.explanation: Energy signals have finite total energy, and their average power over infinite time is zero.

partA.text: The impulse response of a stable LTI system must be:
partA.explanation: BIBO stability requires the impulse response h(t) to be absolutely integrable/summable.

partA.text: The transfer function of a system is defined as the ratio of:
options: Input to output in time domain
Laplace transform of output to input with zero initial conditions
Output to input at steady state only
partA.explanation: Transfer function G(s) = L[output]/L[input] assuming zero initial conditions.

partA.text: A system is said to be stable if all poles of its transfer function lie:
options: In the right half of the s-plane
In the left half of the s-plane
partA.explanation: For BIBO stability, all poles of the transfer function must lie in the left half of the s-plane.

partA.text: The Routh-Hurwitz criterion is used to determine:
options: The frequency response of a system
The number of poles in the right half s-plane
partA.explanation: Routh-Hurwitz criterion determines system stability by counting sign changes indicating RHP poles.

partA.text: In a unity feedback control system, the steady-state error for a step input depends on the:
partA.explanation: For a type-0 system, steady-state error to a step input is determined by the position error constant Kp.

partA.text: The phase margin of a control system is a measure of:
partA.explanation: Phase margin indicates relative stability — how close the system is to instability.

partA.text: A PID controller combines:
partA.explanation: PID = Proportional + Integral + Derivative control actions combined.

partA.text: The root locus technique is used to study the variation of closed-loop poles with respect to:
partA.explanation: Root locus shows how closed-loop pole locations move as a parameter, typically gain K, varies from 0 to ∞.

partA.text: A type-1 system has how many poles at the origin in its open-loop transfer function?
partA.explanation: System type is defined by the number of poles at the origin (integrators); type-1 has exactly one.

partA.text: Bode plot magnitude is typically expressed in:
partA.explanation: Bode magnitude plots express gain in decibels: 20 log10|G(jω)|.

partA.text: In amplitude modulation, the bandwidth of the AM signal is:
partA.explanation: AM bandwidth = 2fm (upper and lower sidebands), twice the message signal bandwidth.

partA.text: Frequency modulation is more resistant to noise than amplitude modulation mainly because:
options: Noise mainly affects amplitude, not frequency
partA.explanation: Since noise primarily affects amplitude, an FM receiver (sensitive to frequency, with amplitude limiting) is more immune to noise.

partA.text: The minimum sampling rate to avoid aliasing when digitizing a signal is called the:
partA.explanation: Nyquist rate = 2 × highest frequency component of the signal, minimum sampling rate to avoid aliasing.

partA.text: Pulse Code Modulation (PCM) involves which three steps in order?
partA.explanation: PCM process order: Sampling the analog signal, Quantizing the samples, then Encoding into binary form.

partA.text: In digital communication, the term 'bit rate' refers to:
options: Number of symbols transmitted per second
Number of bits transmitted per second
partA.explanation: Bit rate is the number of bits transmitted per unit time (bps), distinct from baud (symbol) rate.

partA.text: Shannon's channel capacity theorem states that channel capacity C is given by:
partA.explanation: Shannon-Hartley theorem: C = B log2(1 + S/N), where B is bandwidth and S/N is signal-to-noise ratio.

partA.text: Time Division Multiplexing (TDM) allows multiple signals to share a channel by:
partA.explanation: TDM interleaves samples of different signals into distinct time slots on a shared channel.

partA.text: The main advantage of digital communication systems over analog is:
options: Better noise immunity and signal regeneration
partA.explanation: Digital signals can be regenerated at repeaters, offering much better noise immunity than analog transmission.

partA.text: A satellite in geostationary orbit appears stationary relative to Earth because its orbital period equals:
partA.explanation: A geostationary orbit has a period matching Earth's rotation (~24 hours), so it appears fixed from the ground.

partA.text: Gauss's law relates electric flux through a closed surface to:
partA.explanation: Gauss's law: total electric flux through a closed surface = enclosed charge / ε0.

partA.text: The unit of electric field intensity is:
partA.explanation: Electric field intensity E is measured in volts per metre (V/m) or equivalently N/C.

partA.text: Skin effect in a conductor causes current to concentrate:
options: At the center of the conductor
Near the surface of the conductor
partA.explanation: At high frequencies, skin effect forces current to flow mainly near the conductor's surface.

partA.text: The characteristic impedance of free space is approximately:
partA.explanation: Intrinsic impedance of free space η0 = √(μ0/ε0) ≈ 377 Ω = 120π Ω.

partA.text: A waveguide, unlike a transmission line, cannot support:
partA.explanation: Hollow metallic waveguides cannot support a pure TEM mode; they support TE and TM modes above cutoff.

partA.text: The polarization of an antenna refers to the orientation of the:
options: Electric field vector of the radiated wave
partA.explanation: Antenna polarization describes the orientation of the radiated wave's electric field vector.

partA.text: Brewster's angle is the angle of incidence at which:
options: Reflected wave is fully polarized (no reflection for one polarization)
partA.explanation: At Brewster's angle, one polarization component is not reflected at all — the reflected light is fully polarized.

partA.text: A quarter-wave transformer is used for:
options: Impedance matching between two different impedances
partA.explanation: A λ/4 transmission line section can transform one impedance to another for matching purposes.

partA.text: The standing wave ratio (VSWR) for a perfectly matched line is:
partA.explanation: A perfectly matched line has no reflections, giving VSWR = 1.

partA.text: The 8085 microprocessor is a:
partA.explanation: The 8085 is a classic 8-bit microprocessor with an 8-bit data bus and 16-bit address bus.

partA.text: In the 8085, the address bus width is 16 bits, which allows addressing of:
partA.explanation: 16-bit address bus can address 2^16 = 65,536 locations = 64 KB.

partA.text: The purpose of the Program Counter (PC) in a microprocessor is to:
options: Store the current instruction being executed
Hold the address of the next instruction to be fetched
Store the result of ALU operations
partA.explanation: PC holds the memory address of the next instruction to fetch, incrementing after each fetch.

partA.text: An interrupt in a microprocessor system is used to:
options: Temporarily divert the CPU to service a specific event
partA.explanation: Interrupts temporarily suspend the main program so the CPU can service a higher-priority event, then resume.

partA.text: The stack in a microprocessor operates on which principle?
partA.explanation: A stack follows LIFO — the last item pushed is the first popped.

partA.text: DMA (Direct Memory Access) is used to:
options: Allow peripherals to access memory directly without CPU intervention for each byte
partA.explanation: DMA lets peripherals transfer data to/from memory directly, bypassing the CPU for each transfer, improving speed.

partA.text: An assembler's primary function is to:
options: Translate high-level language to machine code
Translate assembly language mnemonics into machine code
partA.explanation: An assembler converts assembly language source code (mnemonics) into machine code.

partA.text: In embedded systems, a watchdog timer is used to:
options: Reset the system if software hangs or malfunctions
partA.explanation: A watchdog timer resets the microcontroller if it isn't periodically 'kicked', recovering from software hangs.

partB.text: If 5 workers can complete a task in 12 days, how many days will 10 workers take to complete the same task?
partB.explanation: Work is inversely proportional to number of workers: 5×12 = 10×x → x = 6 days.

partB.text: A train travels 300 km in 5 hours. What is its average speed?
Find the next number in the series: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
If CODE is written as DPEF, how is WORD written in the same code?
partB.explanation: Each letter is shifted forward by 1: W→X, O→P, R→S, D→E → XPSE.

partB.text: A is the father of B. B is the sister of C. C is the son of D. How is D related to A?
partB.explanation: A is father of B and C (siblings), and D is the parent of C — so D is A's spouse (wife).

partB.text: Statement: All pens are books. All books are papers. Conclusion: All pens are papers.
partB.explanation: This is a valid syllogism: All A are B, All B are C, therefore All A are C.

partB.text: Which figure completes the series in a rotation pattern where a shape turns 90° clockwise each step? (Assume standard rotation logic)
options: The shape rotated 90° further clockwise from the previous figure
A mirror image of the shape
partB.explanation: In a consistent 90° clockwise rotation series, the next figure continues rotating 90° clockwise from the last one.

partB.text: Look at this series: 7, 10, 8, 11, 9, 12, ? What number should come next?
partB.explanation: Two interleaved series: +3,-2 alternating: 7,10,8,11,9,12,10 — next is 10.

partB.text: A dice has numbers 1-6. If the sum of numbers on opposite faces is always 7, what is opposite to 4?
Pointing to a photograph, a man said, 'She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son.' How is the woman related to the man?
partB.explanation: Grandfather's only son is the man's father, and the daughter of the man's father is his sister.

partB.text: If the day before yesterday was Thursday, what day will it be tomorrow?
partB.explanation: Day before yesterday = Thursday, so today = Saturday, tomorrow = Sunday.

partB.text: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 20 and 30 minutes respectively. If both are opened together, how long will they take to fill the tank?
Choose the odd one out: Triangle, Square, Circle, Cube
partB.explanation: Triangle, Square, and Circle are 2D shapes; Cube is a 3D solid — the odd one out.

partB.text: A man walks 5 km north, then 3 km east, then 5 km south. How far is he from his starting point?
partB.explanation: Net displacement: 5 km north and 5 km south cancel out, leaving only 3 km east.
